lit.\u0027¿Cuáles son T y P del punto triple: "What are T and P of the triple point of water?"
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003ePunto triple\u003c/b\: "Triple point: three phases, F = 0. Critical point: the liquid–gas curve ends."
lit.\u0027\u003cdiv class=\"calc-step\"\u003:
"
2 · Points and curves at that pressure
"
lit.\u0027\u003cp class=\"muted small\"\u003:
"

The curves are fits to experimental data (extended Antoine and Clapeyron); the values are approximate. Use the logarithmic P scale to cover many orders of magnitude.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl punto triple del C:
"

The triple point of CO₂ is at 5.1 atm, above atmospheric pressure: at 1 atm there is no liquid CO₂; the solid (dry ice) sublimes at 194.7 K (−78.5 °C). To obtain liquid CO₂ it must be compressed above 5.1 atm, as in a fire extinguisher.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el \u003cb\u003epu:
"

At the triple point solid, liquid and gas coexist. For water: 273.16 K and 611.657 Pa (0.006 atm); for CO₂: 216.55 K and 517 kPa (5.1 atm). According to the phase rule F = C − P + 2 = 1 − 3 + 2 = 0: no degrees of freedom, the point is unique. That is why the triple point of water defined the kelvin until 2019.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa curva de vaporizac:
"

The vaporization curve ends at the critical point (water: 647.1 K and 22.06 MPa; CO₂: 304.1 K and 7.38 MPa). On approaching it, the liquid expands and the gas densifies until the meniscus disappears. Above Tc and Pc there is a supercritical fluid: liquid density, gas diffusivity (supercritical CO₂ decaffeinates coffee).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa curva sólido–líqui:
"

The solid–liquid curve of water has a negative slope: ice is less dense than liquid water (ΔVfus < 0) and, by Clapeyron dP/dT = ΔH/(TΔV), increasing P favors the liquid. At −1.5 °C ice melts if about 20 MPa is applied. In almost all other substances the slope is positive.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLas curvas separan re:
"

The curves separate regions: melting (solid–liquid), vaporization (liquid–gas) and sublimation (solid–gas). On them, two phases coexist in dynamic equilibrium. The vaporization curve is the vapor pressure as a function of T; the point where it equals 1 atm is the normal boiling point (water: 373.15 K). Here we follow that curve: the liquid and the gas coexist at each T with its vapor P.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUna \u003cb\u003efase:
"

A phase is a homogeneous portion of matter. For a pure substance, the most stable state depends on the temperature and the pressure. We heat water at 1 atm: the solid (ordered particles that vibrate) turns into liquid (disordered but compact) and then into gas (widely separated particles). The phase diagram is the map of P versus T showing which phase is stable at each point.

"
